title: Efficient and Transferable Agentic Knowledge Graph RAG via Reinforcement Learning
claim: Prior KG-RAG uses costly multi-module LLM pipelines tied to one graph; ours uses one multi-turn RL agent that is cheaper and transfers across graphs.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: task setup, red prior workflow with ✗, green ours with ✓
description: Three panels separated by vertical lines. The left panel introduces KG-RAG. A Qwen bear mascot (the language model) is joined by a plus sign to a knowledge-graph icon. Below are a blue Query box ("What did James K. Polk do before he was president?") and a yellow Response box ("Tennessee's governor"). The middle panel has a red-tinted border and is titled "Multi-Module Workflow (Prior Works)". It shows a cycle of Q, Retrieval, Reasoning, Reviewing, Responding and A, each step drawn as a different bear. A large red X and the notes "Computation-Heavy" and "KG-specific Optimization" mark it as the weaker option. The right panel has a green border and a gold star, and is titled "KG-R1: Multi-Turn Agentic Framework (Ours)". One bear agent loops through multi-turn interaction with a Knowledge Graph Query Server. The server shows a list of actions such as get_tail_entities, and a red bracket reads "Optimize with RL". A green check mark and the notes "Cost-efficient Inference" and "Cross-KG Transferability" mark it as the stronger option.
caption: Overview of KG-R1, a multi-turn agentic KG-RAG framework. The framework enables cost-efficient inference and demonstrates strong cross-KG transferability.
abstract: Knowledge-graph retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) couples large language models (LLMs) with structured, verifiable knowledge graphs (KGs) to reduce hallucination and provide reasoning traces. However, current KG-RAG systems often rely on fixed pipelines of multiple LLM modules (e.g., planning, reasoning, and responding), which inflate inference costs and tie performance to specific graph schemas. To address this, we introduce KG-R1, an agentic framework that optimizes KG-RAG through reinforcement learning (RL). Unlike modular workflows, KG-R1 uses a single agent that interacts with KGs as its environment, learning to retrieve information at each step and incorporating it into its reasoning and generation in a unified process. Across Knowledge-Graph Question Answering (KGQA) benchmarks, KG-R1 demonstrates both efficiency and transferability-using Qwen 2.5-3B, KG-R1 improves answer accuracy with fewer generation tokens than prior multi-module workflow methods that use much larger foundation or fine-tuned models. Furthermore, KG-R1 exhibits strong plug-and-play capability: after training, maintaining accuracy on unseen KGs without retraining. These properties make KG-R1 a promising KG-RAG framework for real-world deployment. Our code is publicly available at github.com/junhongmit/KG-R1/.
